`req-03` and the answered `q-04` explicitly limit the operator, Telegram bridge and system-message exemption to a proven identity through `req-10`, never a bypass a seat can claim. Its acceptance criterion requires claimed operator/bridge/system senders to receive no exemption (`docs/project/prds/003-seat-permissions.dd.json:103-109,220-225`).

`req-10` separately rejects machine-key-only caller proof and requires the claimed caller's privately bootstrapped incarnation capability before identity-dependent authority checks. The clarified done_when and workstream s01 do not confuse the caller with the operation's target (`PRD:173-181`; `docs/project/workstreams/003-seat-permissions.dd.json:23-30`). Reading these requirements together, a label or the machine bearer alone cannot establish an exempt origin.

`req-04` requires `--force` with a reason and one spine event naming sender, recipient, policy and reason; its done_when requires the audit event and reason. This is the q-02 outbound-policy override, not an exemption from req-10 authentication (`PRD:113-119`). The workstream carries proven-only exemptions and audited forced sends into s04, which still depends on s03 and thereby s01. Removing answered-question waits does not remove the authentication dependency.

The rendered changes retain the same constraints. All requirements remain planned; s01 remains in-progress and permission steps remain planned. This PR answers policy questions, not implementation or deployed enforcement.
